name: Database activity management
description: Setting up a Database activity: creating and configuring the database, defining its fields (the columns every entry is filled in against), and customising the display templates.
instructions:
A database is built in order: create the module, add every field in one x_mod_data_create_fields call in their final display order (order is creation order and can never be changed; a different display arrangement is achieved by placing the field tags differently in the templates), then adjust templates only if the default layout is not enough. Read current state first: x_mod_data_pre_update for settings and fields, x_mod_data_templates_pre_update for templates.

Field names are the labels participants see; write them in natural language. The description is optional and invisible in the default templates. Field settings travel as raw param columns. Meanings per type (params not listed are unused; leave them out):
- Single line of text (text): param1 = 1 lets the auto-linking filter link occurrences of the value elsewhere in the course.
- Rich text (textarea): param2 = editor width in columns (the form default is 60), param3 = height in rows (default 35), param5 = largest embedded file in bytes (0 = course limit), and param4 is always 1 (a form constant; set it too).
- Number (number): param1 = decimal places shown (integer, 0 or more); empty shows the value exactly as entered. Moodle's own field form does not expose this param.
- Date (date): no params.
- Dropdown, one choice (menu): param1 = the choices, one per line.
- Radio buttons, one choice (radiobutton): param1 = the choices, one per line.
- Selection list, several choices (multimenu): param1 = the choices, one per line.
- Checkboxes, several choices (checkbox): param1 = the choices, one per line.
- Web address (url): param1 = 1 shows it as a clickable link, param2 = fixed link text shown instead of the address, param3 = 1 opens it in a new window.
- Uploaded file (file): param3 = largest upload in bytes (0 = course limit).
- Image (picture): param1 and param2 = display width and height in pixels in single entry view, param4 and param5 = the same for list view, param3 = largest upload in bytes. All optional with no defaults; empty shows the image at its own size.
- Coordinates (latlong): param1 = comma-separated map services offered as links beside the value, chosen from: Google Maps, Google Earth, Geabios, OpenStreetMap, Multimap. param2 = what labels placemarks in the KML export: -1 the entry number, -2 the coordinates, or the id of a text field of this database.
- Email address (email, when installed): no params.
- Pattern-checked text (regex, when installed): param3 = the regular expression a value must match (required), param2 = 1 makes it case sensitive, param4 = 1 allows a partial match, param5 = custom error message shown when a value fails; param1 is obsolete.

Templates: ten columns render the database. listtemplate shows one entry in the list view (listtemplateheader and listtemplatefooter wrap the list), singletemplate one entry on its own page, addtemplate the entry form, asearchtemplate the advanced search form, rsstemplate and rsstitletemplate the feed, csstemplate and jstemplate styling and behaviour. For a field named 'Field title': [[Field title]] renders its value (in addtemplate its input, and a field tag may appear at most once there); [[Field title#name]], [[Field title#description]] and, in addtemplate only, [[Field title#id]] render field metadata; ##tags## such as ##edit##, ##delete##, ##approve##, ##more##, ##user##, ##timeadded##, ##tags## render actions and entry metadata. x_mod_data_templates_pre_update lists exactly which placeholders each template takes, with the current and default content. An empty template column regenerates its default from the current fields on every view, so most databases need no template editing; prefer reset over hand-writing. New fields are appended automatically to customised single, add and RSS templates but never to a customised listtemplate; reset or edit that one after adding fields.

Approval: approval = 1 holds each new entry back until it is approved (mod_data_approve_entry approves or rejects by entry id), and manageapproved = 0 additionally locks an approved entry against its author's edits; manageapproved only applies while approval = 1. Entry limits: maxentries caps how many entries each participant may add, requiredentriestoview hides other people's entries until the participant has added that many, timeavailablefrom and timeavailableto open and close the database, and the timeview pair bounds a read-only period.
